claim: The Maare-Mosel-Radweg runs ~58 km from Daun to Bernkastel-Kues, mostly on a former railway line, asphalted with gentle gradients, featuring viaducts, tunnels and Eifel maar viewpoints.
quote: The route runs entirely on the former railway line from Daun to Lieser... continuously asphalted path has hardly any inclines but plenty of opportunities to rest and sights: two viaducts, numerous bridges, four tunnels, as well as Eifel maars and extinct volcanoes.

claim: A circular hike around all three Dauner Maare from Schalkenmehren is ~9.5 km (5.9 mi), moderate, ~1,145 ft elevation gain, takes 3–3.5 hours.
quote: A moderate hike covers 5.9 mi, with an elevation gain of 1,145 ft, taking about 3–3.5 hr to complete... begins at the Schalkenmehren bus stop and then leads in several laps around the three unique volcanic lakes.

claim: The 11-metre Dronketurm stands on the 561 m Mäuseberg between Weinfelder and Schalkenmehrener Maar; 43 steps lead to panoramic views over the three Dauner Maare and on clear days as far as the Hunsrück and Nürburg.
quote: the eleven-meter-high tower... 43 steps... a wonderful view awaits you of the Gemünden Maar... on the plateau on the 561-metre-high Mäuseberg

claim: The Lieserpfad runs ~74 km in four daily stages of 15–21 km, from the Lieser source near Boxberg to the Mosel at Lieser; took 2nd place in Germany's most beautiful hiking trail vote in 2018.
quote: The 74 km long Lieser Trail can be easily completed in four daily stages between 15 and 21 km in length... In 2018, the Lieserpfad achieved 2nd place as Germany's most beautiful hiking trail!

claim: Lieserpfad Stage 3 Manderscheid–Wittlich is ~23 km with ~760 m elevation gain, the trail's longest stage, passing the Manderscheid castles and steep Lieser valley.

The Burgenklettersteig Manderscheid is the only via ferrata in Rhineland-Palatinate, ~4.6 km in three stages with difficulties A–D including a 60 m rope bridge; equipment (helmet, harness, set) can be rented at the GesundLand Tourist-Information Kurhaus.

The Manderscheider Burgenstieg with Rittersteig is a 5.4 km family-friendly loop through the Lieser valley with the Belvedere lookout offering classic views of both castle ruins (Niederburg, Oberburg).
quote: With a distance of 5.4 kilometres, it is also a popular hike for families. It runs around Manderscheid into the romantic Lieser valley and up to the Belvedere lookout point.

claim: Eifelsteig Stage 11 Daun–Manderscheid is ~20–23 km with ~700 m elevation gain (hard), passing all three Daun Maare before descending into the Lieser valley to Manderscheid.
quote: The trail covers 20.4 km with an elevation gain of 702 m and takes about 6.5–7 hours to complete... starts in Daun and first leads to the Daun maars.

claim: Moselsteig Stage 11 Bernkastel-Kues–Ürzig is 15 km with ~680 m climb, featuring the Maria Zill viewpoint at ~400 m a.s.l. — one of the highest panoramic spots on the entire Moselsteig.
quote: At an altitude of around 400 m above sea level, it is one of the highest and most comprehensive viewing points of the Moselsteig Trail.

claim: Dreis bei Wittlich sits 7 km northeast of Wittlich, ~29 km north of Daun and ~14 km southwest of Schweich, placing the Dauner Maare, Manderscheid and Bernkastel-Kues all inside the 30 km radius.
quote: Dreis bei Wittlich is 7 km northeast of Wittlich, 29 km north of Daun

claim: The VulkaMaar Trail (Vulkaneifel-Pfad) won 'Germany's Most Beautiful Hiking Trail' in 2021 and passes the Meerfelder Maar and the Windsborn Crater Lake (Germany's only above-ground crater lake) plus the Wolfsschlucht ravine.
quote: The VulkaMaar Trail was voted Germany's most beautiful hiking trail in 2021... passing by maars like the Meerfelder Maar and the Windsborn Crater Lake, and traversing areas like the Wolfsschlucht ravine.

claim: The HeimatSpur 'MaareGlück' premium short trail is 11 km and links all three water-filled Daun Maare plus the Schalkenmehrener fen and dry maar.
quote: The HeimatSpur MaareGlück trail covers 11 km and includes water-filled maars, a fen and a dry maar at Schalkenmehren.
